chunks.content: ## Importing and Preparing Pattern Files in CLO This section covers the process of importing DXF pattern files, managing versions of garment panels, and arranging them properly in the 2D and 3D windows within CLO. Key terms include DXF import, pattern version management, 2D/3D window arrangement, and adjustment panel tool. - Enter the library window and navigate to the required files: open the *FemaleVR* folder, double-click the *FVR Feifei* file and drag it into the 3D window. - Similarly, open the *Practice Files* folder, double-click *B-Basic*, then *C-Tissue*, and finally *Shoot*, or drag them directly into the 3D window. - Click **OK** to import the DXF file. - Use the **Adjustment Panel Tool** to manage pattern pieces on the 2D grid. - Select all versions of the front panel (e.g., Shoukofu and Shouchatiao), and place them adjacent to the Shou piece. - Likewise, select the Fanling and LiLing versions of the shirt and position them next to the DaShengBeibu version. - Arrange the T-shirt pattern pieces around the virtual model shadow in the 2D window. - Since only half of the clothing pattern versions are provided, duplicate the other half using the adjustment panel tool. - For the back panel, right-click and select **Edit Folder Line**, open the back page, then select all back panels except the collar. - Right-click the panel and choose options for **Column-linked**, **Symmetrical version**, and **Sewing line**. - Hold **Shift** and place the duplicated version aligned symmetrically on the opposite side. - In the 3D window, use **Rearrange 2D Arrangement Position > All** to sync the 2D and 3D pattern pieces. ## Aligning and Arranging Pattern Pieces on the Model This section explains how to align, rotate, and arrange front, back, and sleeve panels precisely using positional balls and arrangement points, crucial for accurate garment construction. - Select the mouse tool in the 3D vertical toolbar (4th position) to display arrangement points on the virtual model. - Open and inspect arrangement points; some may be blocked and require adjustment. - In the 2D window, select all panels with **Ctrl+J** and move them to free blocked arrangement points. - For panels with layers (e.g., front panels), select the right front panel, use the positional ball tool to pull and align it with the upper left front panel. - Rotate the 3D view to check for gaps between panels. - Repeat this process for sleeve panels, positioning sleeves correctly on the arm arrangement points. - Use shortcut key **8** to view the model from the rear. - Select the back preview and back panel simultaneously in the 2D window, then place them on the back view arrangement point in 3D. - Place the wrist panel on the corresponding wrist arrangement point. - Use shortcut key **2** to return to the front view. - In the 3D toolbar, toggle the display of arrangement points and hide the model arrangement point for better visibility.

chunks.content: - Use shortcut key **8** to view the model from the rear. - Select the back preview and back panel simultaneously in the 2D window, then place them on the back view arrangement point in 3D. - Place the wrist panel on the corresponding wrist arrangement point. - Use shortcut key **2** to return to the front view. - In the 3D toolbar, toggle the display of arrangement points and hide the model arrangement point for better visibility. ## Line Alignment and Embroidery Preparation This section details the use of line alignment tools for precise matching of garment parts and the preparation of embroidery lines, including cutting, adjusting, and setting fold angles. - Use the **Line Alignment Tool** in the 2D window to align front and rear garment edges, paying close attention to alignment directions. - Align sleeve and arm panels similarly. - Use the **N-Line Alignment Tool** when dealing with pointy or curved lines. - Select the sleeve line first, hold **Shift**, then select the arm line, and release Shift after alignment. - Use the **Cut** function by right-clicking the blue baseline to cut inner lines on the embroidery board. - Adjust the length of the new outline by dragging the cut tool. - Use **Undo Shift** on the blue baseline representing the embroidered bar and press **Return** to hook the baseline to the inner line. - Employ the **Line Embroidery Tool** to sew the embroidered bar onto the sleeve bar. - When sewing, ensure the embroidered bar is open on one side and avoid sewing parts of the bar directly onto the sleeve. - Use the **Collar Expansion Tool** to create inner lines by selecting the two blue baselines farthest from the embroidered bar and pressing **Return** to convert them. - In the 2D window, select the **Embroidered Bar Tool**, choose the inner line farthest from the embroidered bar, and set fold angles in the attribute editor: - One inner line: fold angle 0 degrees - Other inner line: fold angle 360 degrees - Apply the **Line Embroidery Tool** for relative embroidery on both sides of the 360-degree line. - Use the **Free Embroidery Tool** for relative embroidery on both ends of the 0-degree line. ## Embroidery Line Types and Simulation This section covers changing embroidery line types and activating simulations to visualize folds and seams realistically. - Select the embroidered line on the sleeve bar and change its type to **Turned** in the attribute editor. - Activate simulation to achieve even folds during garment draping. - Use the **Free Embroidery Tool** to divide the bottom of the sleeve bar strip and the sleeve, ensuring the side remains open without merging the sleeve bar strip with the sleeve. - Set the embroidered line type to **Turned** again for consistent folds. - Merge the sleeve bar strip onto the sleeve using the **Free Embroidery Tool**. - Create an embroidered line on the sleeve bar strip, sewing from right to left.

chunks.content: - Activate simulation to achieve even folds during garment draping. - Use the **Free Embroidery Tool** to divide the bottom of the sleeve bar strip and the sleeve, ensuring the side remains open without merging the sleeve bar strip with the sleeve. - Set the embroidered line type to **Turned** again for consistent folds. - Merge the sleeve bar strip onto the sleeve using the **Free Embroidery Tool**. - Create an embroidered line on the sleeve bar strip, sewing from right to left. - After completing the first half of sewing, sew the second half while holding **Shift** to create a sewing line on the sleeve strip. - Maintain consistent sewing line direction throughout to avoid twisting. - Use the **Twist Tool** in the 3D toolbar to correct any twisting issues. ## Button and Buttonhole Creation and Management This section explains creating, copying, pasting, and positioning buttonholes and buttons on garment panels, including how to synchronize them on symmetrical panels. - Blue baseline marks on panels indicate button or buttonhole locations. - Click once on the panel to create a buttonhole line in the 2D panel and a corresponding buttonhole image in 3D. - Use the **Move Buttonhole Tool** in the 3D toolbar to select and position buttonholes. - Right-click a buttonhole in the 2D window to copy and paste it. - Use **Shift + drag** to align buttonholes vertically. - Access the dialogue window by right-clicking on the baseline to specify the number of buttons, then click **OK** to create multiple buttonholes. - To synchronize buttonholes on symmetrical panels, right-click the buttonhole and select the option to support symmetry. - Align buttonholes by right-clicking and selecting the alignment option. - Left-click the buttonhole to finalize. - Draw seam allowances and tassels on embroidered sections multiple times as needed. - Use the button join function ("17 button") to link buttons and marks, locking the points as necessary. - Copy buckles and buttons via right-click menu and adjust buckle angles and positions in the shape editor. - Add and tighten buckles on collars using the same method. - Fold front and center collars, right-click the menu, and select the direction for buckles to face outward. ## Fold Arrangement and Inner Line Settings This section describes creating fold lines, setting fold angles, and activating simulations to control garment folding behavior. - In the 2D window, use the **Edit Tool** to select the bottom line of the panel. - Right-click and select the inner line as the border. - Enter the fold distance in the dialog box and confirm. - In the 3D toolbar, select the **Fold Arrangement Tool** and click on the newly created inner line on the 3D costume. - The fold arrangement positioning tool will appear, showing fold directions. - For precise folding, set the fold angle of the inner line to 360 degrees using the **Edit Sheet Tool** in the 2D toolbar. - Activate simulation to visualize folds; click again to close the simulation.

Select the created model in the window to finalize the setup.
